title: Gibraltar’s Famous Monkeys Are Eating Dirt, Likely to Alleviate Stomach Aches From Munching on Tourists’ Junk Food
titleZh: 猴群、垃圾食品与“食土行为”
summary:
先别急着吃胃药了。直布罗陀的猴子似乎发现了一个缓解肠胃不适的另类健康窍门。研究人员在3月19日发表于《科学报告》期刊的一项研究中指出，这片英国海外领地上的标志性猕猴，已经学会通过吃土来缓解因食用游客投喂——或从游客手中抢夺——的零食而引发的消化问题。英国剑桥大学灵长类行为生态学家、论文合著者西尔万·勒穆瓦纳在接受科技媒体Gizmodo采访时表示，这项研究“为理解这些灵长类种群如何在高度人为干扰的环境中生存适应，提供了新的视角。”

来源：史密森尼；作者：Sara Hashemi；原文发布时间：2026-04-24 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Move over, Tums. Monkeys in Gibraltar seem to have found an unusual health hack to deal with upset stomachs. The British territory’s famous macaques have learned to eat dirt to help with digestion issues caused by eating snacks given by—or stolen from—tourists, researchers report in a study published March 19 in the journal Scientific Reports. The work “sheds light on the adaptability of these primate populations living in highly anthropogenic landscapes,” says study co-author Sylvain Lemoine, a primate behavioral ecologist at the University of Cambridge in England, to Ed Cara at Gizmodo.
paragraphs.contentZh: 先别急着吃胃药了。直布罗陀的猴子似乎发现了一个缓解肠胃不适的另类健康窍门。研究人员在3月19日发表于《科学报告》期刊的一项研究中指出，这片英国海外领地上的标志性猕猴，已经学会通过吃土来缓解因食用游客投喂——或从游客手中抢夺——的零食而引发的消化问题。英国剑桥大学灵长类行为生态学家、论文合著者西尔万·勒穆瓦纳在接受科技媒体Gizmodo采访时表示，这项研究“为理解这些灵长类种群如何在高度人为干扰的环境中生存适应，提供了新的视角。”

paragraphs.contentEn: About 230 Barbary macaques live on Gibraltar, located at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula, bordering Spain. They’re the only wild monkeys currently residing in Europe, and they were likely introduced by humans long ago. The animals have divided themselves into eight stable groups that live on different areas of the territory’s well-known mountain, the Rock of Gibraltar. Tourists flock to see the monkeys, and that contact with humans leads to them feast on ice cream, bread, cookies and other snacks that are calorie-rich but fiber-poor—even though they’re fed fruit and vegetables every day by local authorities.
paragraphs.contentZh: 直布罗陀位于伊比利亚半岛最南端，毗邻西班牙，这里生活着约230只巴巴里猕猴。它们是欧洲目前唯一的野生猴种，普遍认为是很早以前由人类引入该地的。这些猕猴已自然分化为八个稳定的族群，分别栖息在当地标志性山体“直布罗陀巨岩”的不同区域。大量游客慕名前来观赏猴群，尽管当地管理部门每天会为它们投喂水果和蔬菜，但与人类的频繁接触，仍使它们有机会接触并食用冰淇淋、面包、饼干等高热量、低纤维的零食。

paragraphs.contentEn: Signs all over the Rock say not to hand out meals to the creatures, but the rules are not well-enforced. Tour guides even offer meals directly to the macaques, encouraging tourists to do it too, wrote BBC Discover Wildlife’s Arnold Monteith. In 2022, Lemoine and his colleagues began conducting a long-term study of the monkeys’ behavior and ecology, per Gizmodo. That’s when they noticed the animals regularly munching on dirt, a practice known as geophagy. Across nearly 100 observation days from August 2022 to April 2024, the researchers witnessed 44 monkeys eating soil a total of 46 times. They also found that junk food made up almost one-fifth of the examined macaques’ diets.
paragraphs.contentZh: 虽然直布罗陀巨岩上随处可见禁止投喂猕猴的告示，但相关规定并未得到严格执行。BBC《探索野生动物》撰稿人阿诺德·蒙泰思指出，部分导游甚至会直接给猕猴喂食，并鼓励游客效仿。据Gizmodo报道，2022年，勒穆瓦纳及其同事开始对这些猕猴的行为与生态展开长期研究。正是在这一过程中，他们注意到这些猕猴会反复啃食土壤，这一行为在学术上被称为食土癖（geophagy）。在2022年8月至2024年4月将近100天的观察期内，研究人员共记录到44只猕猴食土，总计发生46次。此外他们还发现，在受测猕猴的饮食结构中，垃圾食品的占比已接近五分之一。

paragraphs.contentEn: A relationship emerged between how much dirt the creatures ate and how frequently they interacted with humans. Macaques near the top of the Rock—an area that sees a lot of tourism—ate the most junk food, as well as the most dirt. Sometimes they even chowed down on soil right after eating a tourist treat. On the other hand, a group that did not have prolonged contact with tourists was never seen engaging in geophagy. When tourist numbers dropped in the winter, the macaques were 40 percent less likely to eat human food and 31 percent less likely to eat soil than in the summer, the team found.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究发现，猕猴食土量的多少与它们同人类接触的频率之间存在关联。盘踞在直布罗陀巨岩顶部一带的猕猴——该区域游客最为密集——摄入的垃圾食品最多，同时食土量也最大。有时，它们甚至会在吃下游客投喂的零食后，立即开始啃食土壤。相比之下，一个长期不与游客接触的猕猴族群，从未被观察到有食土行为。研究团队还发现，随着冬季游客数量减少，猕猴食用人类食物的可能性较夏季下降了40%，食土的可能性也降低了31%。

paragraphs.contentEn: “We think the macaques started eating soil to buffer their digestive system against the high-energy, low-fiber nature of these snacks and junk foods, which have been shown to cause gastric upsets in some primates,” Lemoine says in a statement. “The consumed soil acts as a barrier in the digestive tract, limiting absorption of harmful compounds. This could alleviate gastrointestinal symptoms from nausea to diarrhea.” Research suggests that geophagy serves many purposes connected to detoxification and supplementing their diets with important minerals, Paula Pebsworth, a primatologist at the University of Texas at San Antonio who was not involved in the study, tells Ian Sample at the Guardian.
paragraphs.contentZh: 勒穆瓦纳在一份声明中表示：“我们认为，猕猴开始食土，是为了在消化系统中形成一种缓冲机制，以应对这些高热量、低纤维零食带来的影响，此前已有研究表明，这类食物可能会在部分灵长类动物中引发胃肠不适。摄入的土壤可在消化道内形成一道屏障，减少有害物质的吸收。从而有助于缓解恶心、腹泻等胃肠道症状。”未参与该研究的德克萨斯大学圣安东尼奥分校灵长类动物学家保拉·佩布斯沃思在接受《卫报》记者伊恩·桑普尔采访时表示，相关研究显示，食土行为可能具有多重功能，包括解毒以及补充日常饮食中缺失的重要矿物质。

paragraphs.contentEn: Lemoine and his colleagues doubt that the monkeys are eating dirt to help with mineral supplementation. If that was the cause, they should have seen pregnant and lactating animals increase their soil intake, which wasn’t observed. Pebsworth says it is plausible that the macaques are engaging in the strange practice to help them digest all the human food, and notes that the practice has been documented at Japan’s Arashiyama Monkey Park. “However, while geophagy may serve as a coping mechanism, a more effective management approach is to reduce or eliminate the provisioning of human foods,” she tells the Guardian.
paragraphs.contentZh: 勒穆瓦纳及其同事并不认为猕猴食土是为了补充矿物质。他们指出，如果确实是为了补充矿物质，那么处于孕期或哺乳期的个体应当会增加土壤摄入量，但研究中并未观察到这一现象。佩布斯沃思则表示，将猕猴这一奇特行为解释为帮助消化人类食物是合理的，她还提到，类似的食土现象在日本岚山猴园也曾有过记录。不过，她在接受《卫报》采访时强调：“尽管食土可能是一种应对机制，但更有效的管理方式仍是减少或彻底杜绝人类投喂。”
